p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram of the regulation of CDK by phosphorylation and proteolysis. In part a, as a cell enters mitosis, the M-hased CDK is inactive. In part b, the active cyclin-CDK complex triggers its own activation by phosphorylation of destruction box recognizing protein (DBRP). The diagram spans two sections; the top part, which is shaded light blue, and the bottom part, which is shaded gray. The diagram is comprised of a series of arrows forming a rectangle. In part a, inactive CDK, represented as a small blue rectangle, is on the border of the two shaded parts. An arrow points up and then turns to the right. Along the way, cyclin, which is represented by a red pill, enters the reaction. The arrow points to the formation of a Cyclin-CDK complex bound to a Tyr-15, which s bound to a red P. Phosphorylated Tyr 15 blocks the ATP binding site on the CDK-cyclin complex, so that remains inactive. Another arrow points to the right and downward, showing the CDK structure with Tyr on both the left and right corners; the one on the left is attached to a red P, and the one on the right is attached to a green P. This structure is still attached to cyclin, and at this point, CDK becomes activated.From here, Pi leaves the equation, and another arrow points downwars to a phosphorylated CDK, which is attached to cycline, Thr, and P. On the left of this structure, there are two dashed arrows pointing to the left of the structure; one arrow points up to a Phosphotase (green oval), which then is phosphorylated by a green P, which then has another dashed arrow pointing to the part of the reaction where Pi leaves. The dashed arrow facing downwars points to a DBRP, which is then shown being phosphorylated by a green P. Another dashed arrow points to the bottom right side of the diagram, where U (ubiquitin ligase) enters the reaction, and the CDK-cyclin complex attaches to four U's. From here, another arrow shows cyclin being degraded, and an arrow pointing upward shows CDK at the starting point.
